chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Perform the daytime prayer at whatever hour you wish, from night or day, all of that is equal."
ai.seo_question: When is the best time to perform the daytime prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of Salat al-Nahar (the daytime prayer), often identified with Zuhr or Asr, by affirming that its validity is not restricted to specific canonical hours but can be performed at any time during the day or night. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (taysir) in worship, allowing believers to fulfill their obligations amidst varying circumstances without compromising the prayer's spiritual integrity. It underscores the importance of intention and consistency over rigid temporal constraints in maintaining daily devotional practices.
